title: Team Access Hub — sketch notes + backlog
body:
Purpose:
Short brain dump and prioritized backlog for a consolidated 'Team Access Hub' in Console — goal is to gather RBAC, API key management, service accounts, and audit log views into a single, discoverable surface that fits Redwood’s enterprise and self-serve personas. This doc captures wireframe intent, flows, known edge cases, and an initial backlog with acceptance criteria.

Context / why now:
- Multiple teams keep asking for a single place to manage team-level access controls (sales, SRE, infra, product).
- Current flows spread across: org admin > keys > service accounts > audit (confusing).
- Dedicated & Private customers need clear service-account onboarding + audit export for compliance.

Personas:
- Org Admin (security-focused): wants clear audit, rotation, export, retention controls.
- Team Lead (product/platform): wants role templates, simple add/remove members, and quick keys for CI.
- Developer (self-serve): wants to create ephemeral API keys, see usage limits, and understand scope.
- Platform/SRE: wants service account lifecycle (create, attach policies, rotate) and automation hooks.

High-level goals:
1) Single entrypoint: "Team Access Hub" with top-level tabs for Roles, API Keys, Service Accounts, and Audit Logs.
2) Make common tasks 1–3 clicks (create role, issue key, rotate key, view last 30d audit).
3) Provide safe defaults and guardrails: key expiry defaults, least-privilege role templates, canary for wide-scope keys.
4) Support enterprise needs: exportable audit CSV, retention policy selector, integrations (SIEM/Splunk).

Wireframe notes (layout + components):
- Header: "Team Access Hub" + team/org selector dropdown (breadcrumb style).
- Left nav: compact 4-item nav (Roles, API Keys, Service Accounts, Audit). Secondary items: Usage, Policies (future).
- Main panel default: Roles list (sorted by usage, then name). Quick actions inline.

Roles tab wireframe (sketch):
- Top toolbar: New Role (primary), Import (CSV/JSON) (secondary), Role templates dropdown.
- Table columns: Role name | Scope (team/org) | Members count | Last used | Attached policies | Actions (edit, clone, delete).
- Role edit modal: name, description (markdown-lite), policy editor (simple toggles + advanced JSON), member list (invite by email + SSO groups), change history link.
- Important microcopy: "Roles are applied at team-level by default. To grant cross-team access, select Org scope — consider adding just the required permissions."

API Keys tab wireframe (sketch):
- Top toolbar: New API key (menu with Ephemeral key, Long-lived key, CI key template).
- Table columns: Key name | Created by | Scope (role or limited scopes) | Expires | Last used | Status (active/rotated) | Actions (revoke, rotate, show)
- New key flow: 1) name 2) scope (role or explicit scopes) 3) expiry (default 90d for long-lived, 1h for ephemeral) 4) restrictions (IP allowlist, referrers) 5) confirm -> show token once.
- UX safeguards: warn when choosing org-scope or "*" scopes; require checkbox confirmation and record in audit reason.

Service Accounts tab wireframe (sketch):
- Top toolbar: New service account (guided) — choose human vs machine distinction in copy.
- Card-based list: name, linked roles/policies, attached keys (count), automated rotation toggle, last rotation date.
- Guided onboarding modal: 1) create SA 2) attach role or attach policy presets (e.g., inference-runner, infra-deploy), 3) create initial key (ephemeral recommended) 4) provide client-id and instructions for K8s secrets or VM injection.
- Suggested microcopy for enterprise: "Service accounts are machine identities. Use short-lived keys and automatic rotation for production workloads."

Audit Log tab wireframe (sketch):
- Header: quick filters (date range, actor, action type, resource, result).
- Results pane: infinite scroll with grouped-by-day entries. Each entry includes actor, action verb, resource, outcome, and link to raw event JSON.
- Actions: export current filter to CSV/NDJSON, configure export integration (S3, Splunk, SIEM webhook) — note: add retention controls UI on this panel or separate policies page.
- Quick insight cards above logs: total events in window, failed auths, keys revoked, role changes.

Accessibility / keyboard flows:
- All modals trap focus; keyboard shortcuts for primary actions (c = create role, k = create key).
- Table rows actionable via Enter; inline actions keyboard reachable.

Error states & edge cases:
- Creating long-lived key without expiry -> show hard stop and require explicit rationale.
- Rotation: ensure keys in use are not immediately revoked until confirm. Provide staged rotation with preview hook.
- Member invite to SAML group not resolvable -> show pending status and link to admin SSO settings.
- Heavy audit window -> pagination fallback for >1M events; warn about export size.

Telemetry + observability requirements (for Console):
- Track: create_key, rotate_key, revoke_key, create_role, edit_role, attach_policy, create_service_account, rotate_service_account_key, audit_export. Include user, IP, client, and request id.
- Surface top risky actions in Product Console: last 30d keys with org-scope, keys with no expiry, service accounts with no rotation.

Backlog (prioritized):
1) [P0] Roles list + create/edit modal + role templates (JIRA-ISSUE-1423) (est 5d). Acceptance: create role + attach to team + assign member -> permission enforced in a sample API call.
2) [P0] API Key create flow (ephemeral + long-lived) + show-once secret UX + revoke/rotate flow (JIRA-ISSUE-1424) (est 8d). Acceptance: token issuance, show-once, rotation toggles backed by backend stub, UI warns on org-scope.
3) [P1] Service account guided creation + initial key issuance + auto-rotation toggle (JIRA-ISSUE-1429) (est 6d). Acceptance: create SA, attach role, create key, rotate via UI.
4) [P1] Audit Log basic filters + export (CSV) + small insight cards (JIRA-ISSUE-1432) (est 5d). Acceptance: apply filters, download CSV <5MB for 30d window.
5) [P2] IP allowlist & referrer restrictions for keys (JIRA-ISSUE-1438) (est 4d).
6) [P2] Bulk role import/export and migration tool for older orgs (JIRA-ISSUE-1460) (est 7d).
7) [P3] SIEM integration (Splunk/S3 webhook) + retention controls (JIRA-ISSUE-1475) (est 8d).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default expiry policy for new orgs (90d vs 30d). Compliance might prefer 30d for enterprise — recommend per-tenant override.
- Should "Org-scope" be behind a permission or require 2-person approval for enterprise? (security asks for approval flows).
- Service account naming convention & labels (enforce unique slug?).
- Backfill audit for existing keys — do we show created-before-telemetry migration? UX needs to surface unknown last-used values.

Prototype links & quick references:
- Figma file: https://figma.com/file/abcd-team-access-hub (current artboard: Access Hub v2)
- Example API for keys: https://api.redwood.ai/docs/#keys-create (dev stub used in prototype)
- Jira epic: JIRA-EPIC-ACCESS-2025

Next steps (short):
- Sync with Security (EOD Thu) to decide org-scope approval requirement (owner: Asha).
- UX studio: turn sketches into clickable Figma frames for flows in P0 items (owner: Miguel).
- Backend: define key-show-once contract and rotation preview endpoint (owner: Evelyn).
- Schedule design review with SRE & Solutions Eng for service-account onboarding edge cases (owner: Tom).

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally pragmatic — we need MVP that prevents footguns (org-scope keys without rationale, keys without expiry) and supports enterprise exports.
- Expect iterations: the audit UI will need performance tuning for large orgs; consider server-side sampling for insights.

Raw brainstorm fragments (keep for context):
- "Make "rotate" produce a second key and keep old key active for 24h to avoid breaking jobs."
- "Show risk score next to each key (derived from scope, age, last used)."
- "When creating a key for CI, prefill CI key template and detect common repo names to suggest mount steps."
- "Add a 'suggested least-privilege' preview when editing role JSON: highlight removed perms vs default template."

-- end of doc --
